title: What the Database Federation is
description: The federation lets many independently run databases answer queries as one, without any of them surrendering control. A query arrives at the federation layer, which plans it across member databases, translates it for each, and combines the results. Members join by signing the compact and publishing their schema and permissions — and they can leave the same way.

title: Cross-database query planning algorithm
description: The planner breaks a federated query into per-member subqueries, decides join order across databases, and pushes filters down to members to minimize data movement. It uses each member's published statistics to estimate costs, and it never asks a member for data its permissions forbid.

title: Schema mediation algorithm
description: Members describe the same things differently — one table's 'title' is another's 'name'. Mediation maps member schemas to the federation's shared model with explicit, tested mappings, and flags unmappable fields instead of guessing. Mappings are versioned so schema evolution does not silently break queries.

title: Federated indexing and retrieval
description: The federation keeps a lightweight global index — which members hold which kinds of records — so the planner can skip irrelevant members without asking them. The global index holds metadata only, never member data, preserving each member's ownership and privacy.

title: Reasoning: permission-aware query answering
description: A federated answer is only valid if the caller was allowed to see every row in it. The executor evaluates permissions per member per caller, filters at the source, and marks the combined answer with the permission context. If a member denies access, the answer says which member was excluded and why.

title: Failure modes: member outages and compact breaches
description: Members go offline, break their schema promises, or quietly change permissions. The federation detects outages, quarantines breaching members automatically, reroutes queries around them, and reports exactly what was missing from each answer. A federation that hides member failures is not a federation but a rumor mill.

description: No central owner means trust must be engineered: signed compacts, authenticated members, query audit trails spanning members, and cost accounting that prevents one member from bankrupting another with expensive queries.
